also: what does that matter to me?
what does it matter to you?

terms.gloss: it is in the interest of, it matters to
terms.grammar: verb: impersonal, from intersum; with meā, tuā or a genitive
evidence: Cic. Fam. 16.4.4: tuā et meā maximē interest tē valēre
terms.comment: With the genitive of the person, or meā, tuā, nostrā, and an infinitive or a clause: illud meā magnī interest, tē ut videam (Cic. Att. 11.22.2, Lewis & Short), it matters a lot to me to see you. How much it matters goes in the genitive: magnī, permagnī, tantī.

evidence: Sen. Ep. 77.20: nōn quam diū, sed quam bene ācta sit, rēfert
Plaut. Curc. 3.25: quid id meā rēfert? (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 103: what does that matter to me (you, us)?, quid id meā (tuā, nōbīs) rēfert?
terms.comment: It makes no difference to me: nīl meā interest or rēfert (Traupman 96).

phrases.latin: tuā et meā maximē interest tē valēre
phrases.english: it matters most to you and to me that you get well

phrases.latin: ergō quid rēfert meā cui serviam, clītellās cum portem meās?
phrases.english: then what difference does it make to me whom I serve, so long as I carry my own packs?

phrases.latin: in gubernandō nihil, in officiō plūrimum interest, quō in genere peccētur
phrases.english: in steering it makes no difference which way you go wrong; in duty it makes all the difference

phrases.latin: quā rē parvī rēfert mē probāre cōgitātiōnem tuam
phrases.english: so it matters little that I approve your plan

phrases.latin: quōmodo fābula, sīc vīta: nōn quam diū, sed quam bene ācta sit, rēfert
phrases.english: as with a play, so with life: what matters is not how long but how well it is acted
